data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Zechariah, which means 'God remembered'. In the Bible, Zechariah was a priest and the father of John the Baptist. data.cultural_impact: The name Zacharie is of Hebrew origin and has been popular among Christians since biblical times. It's a name with a rich history and cultural significance that evokes images of faith and remembrance. The name was particularly prominent during the Middle Ages in Europe, and many notable figures bearing the name have left their mark on history.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Zacharie lies in its biblical roots. Zacharie is the name of a man who, despite his advanced age, was chosen by God to be the father of John the Baptist, a key figure in the story of salvation. The name serves as a reminder that no matter how old we may be, or how seemingly insignificant our role in life may seem, God still remembers us and can work through us to bring about great things. It's a reminder of the power of faith and the importance of remembering that God always has a plan, even when we may not understand it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zacharie means "God remembers" in Hebrew. This name symbolizes the faith and trust in God's promises, even when they seem forgotten. It is a reminder that God keeps His covenants and never abandons His people.

biblical_reference.note: the biblical reference is to the priest Zachariah, son of Jeiel and a descendant of Aaron

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that In the New Testament, Zacharie is the name of the father of John the Baptist. The name Zacharie carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
